data.exact_reserve_text: The increase in the net loss ratio to 86.5% (2018: 81.8%) reflects a number of large losses including the impact of Typhoons Faxai and Hagibis on the Treaty book, a large satellite loss and the grounding of Boeing 737 Max 8 impacting the Space/Aviation book plus reserve strengthening within the casualty classes. This year [2017 YOA] has closed at a loss of GBP 34.0m. The 2018 year of account is expected to close by way of reinsurance to close into its successor year of account at the normal 36-month period and is forecast to make a loss to ultimate of GBP 25.2m.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported an overall gross prior year reserve release of GBP 86.77 million, representing a 61.09% reduction in opening gross claims outstanding. This release is calculated from the gross claims development table for underwriting years 2015, 2016, and 2017. Despite this overall release, the report notes "reserve strengthening within the casualty classes" contributing to an increase in the net loss ratio. The 2017 year of account closed at a loss of GBP 34.0 million, and the 2018 year of account is forecast to close at a loss of GBP 25.2 million, indicating adverse overall underwriting results for those prior years, which may include some adverse claims development not fully captured by the gross claims development table's overall movement. The report also mentions several large losses impacting the current year's loss ratio, including Typhoons Faxai and Hagibis on the Treaty book, a large satellite loss, and the grounding of Boeing 737 Max 8 affecting the Space/Aviation book.
